misconceptions.description: Saving files as 'Untitled.docx' or 'final final v2' so the name does not say what the file contains or proves
misconceptions.trigger: file names do not describe content or the claim they support
misconceptions.feedback: Rename each file so the name states the content (for example 02_factcheck_table.xlsx). A reviewer should not have to open it to know what it is.

misconceptions.description: Collecting a pile of files with no manifest linking each file to the specific claim it proves
misconceptions.trigger: folder has files but no map from file to claim
misconceptions.feedback: Build a manifest: one row per file naming the claim it supports. A claim with no file is unsupported; a file with no claim is clutter.

misconceptions.description: Padding the folder with extra files (a stray screenshot) that prove nothing, assuming more files mean stronger evidence
misconceptions.trigger: folder includes items that map to no claim
misconceptions.feedback: Cut files that prove nothing on their own. Evidence strength comes from each file backing a claim, not from the file count.

misconceptions.description: Renaming or keeping only the final file and claiming it proves revision happened, when no before/after evidence exists.
misconceptions.trigger: a claim of revision is backed by a single saved version
misconceptions.feedback: Save both versions (persona_v1.txt and persona_v2.txt) or drop the claim. A single final file, whatever it is named, cannot back 'I revised it'; the evidence of revision is the pair a reviewer can compare.

misconceptions.description: Keeping an AI-suggested claim in the evidence package when its source cannot be verified.
misconceptions.trigger: an AI-drafted statistic or citation enters the manifest without a verification row
misconceptions.feedback: Every AI suggestion that touches the evidence package gets a decision-log row: accepted with its verified source, or rejected with the reason it could not be verified. An unverifiable statistic is rejected, not softened.
